title: Quarterly lane allocation playbook for Hosted API + model catalog with surge simulation
creator: Nina Alvarez
description: Objective: Produce a compact, operational playbook that maps quarterly lane allocations (commitment lanes, buffer lanes, and emergent surge lanes) for the Hosted API model catalog and validate the plan via simulated surge runs. This ticket covers: 1) a decision framework for assigning models to lanes based on cost/latency/criticality; 2) concrete lane capacity allocations tied to OKRs and committed SLAs; 3) automated surge simulation harness and dashboard validation; 4) canary windows and rollback runbooks to be used during rotation and onboarding; 5) handoff checklist for SRE and runtime engineering. Outcome: a playbook and a set of validated runbook artifacts that the capacity team can use to make quarterly lane decisions and trigger safe rotations.
acceptance_criteria: Lane allocation decision matrix reviewed and approved by PM+Eng (doc link present)
Surge simulation executed for two representative traffic profiles with pass/fail metrics recorded
Dashboard panels created for surge runs: P99 latency, tail OOMs, queue depth, cost per token
Canary runbook and rollback checklist published and tested in staging
Post-simulation debrief recorded with action items assigned to ENG/SRE/Console teams
decisions: Reserve a 20% buffer lane capacity for emergent surge across the fleet
Adopt 24-hour canary windows for model rotations that change quantization or kernel paths
Use prefix-based routing to separate latency-sensitive customers into high-priority lanes
Require a 95th-percentile quality check on the evaluation set before production promotion
